desc:
This jump prevents White from blocking at **R15**. (Vol. 1.) Nowadays, many professionals leave the joseki unfinished to play in the upper left. See [Cho Yeonwoo---Let's master 3-4 point joseki](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WrawM8besGQ&t=57). is played most of the time.
is also joseki.
shows a common probe against Black's corner. White might choose a more active move and [approach a Black 4-4 stone with and continue with the attachment joseki](24025). It is also common to attach to a Black shimari in the upper left [like this](29512) or [this](29494).
